newsitem.title: UK: Brent paper jumps, wet talked firm on Iraq absence.
newsitem.headline: Brent paper jumps, wet talked firm on Iraq absence.

text.p: Brent paper traded firmer on Friday while physical grades were offered at steady to stronger numbers, traders said.
Traders attributed the early strength to the market's renewed focus on lingering uncertainty over a resumption date for Iraqi exports following the end of the OPEC meeting in Vienna.
"Fundamentally the market looks pretty good until Iraq comes out. And it hasn't come out yet," one trader said.
"There isn't enough oil about short-term," said another.
Paper was markedly more active than the last two days of moribund play. Brent July/August traded two cents stronger at -19 cents and was rumoured done also at -15 and -16 cents.
Brent swaps were dicussed six cents stronger for next week and the week after.

Contracts for Difference for June 30-July 4 were talked at August Brent -30/-29 cents and July 7-11 at -32/-31 cents. Periods further out were not talked as traders focussed on rising short-term values.
A wet Brent was offered at August Brent -15 cents on Thursday -- 10 cents above the last reported trade -- and some traders felt the offer would firm further on Friday.
Forties traded at least four times on Thursday at healthily steady numbers. One cargo loading more than a month away on July 29-31 changed hands at Dated +33 cents.
Outright values firmed. August Brent IPE futures rose 13 cents to trade at $17.98 at 0945 GMT in what brokers said was quiet, technical-led trade.
The single wet Brent due to turn wet on Thursday was late passed to Stasco by Cargill, a trader said.
The pass was made after a dispute between Cargill and Esso over the status of the July 11-13 loader.
